newsitem.title: INDIA: Separatists blast key bridge in north-east India.
newsitem.headline: Separatists blast key bridge in north-east India.

text.p: Tribal guerrillas blew up a bridge that forms the main link between India's northeast regions and the rest of the country, injuring seven people, police said on Monday.

A police officer told Reuters that ethnic Bodo rebels blasted the bridge over a small river at Rakhaldubi, between the towns of Bijni and Bongaigaon on National Highway 31 in the tea and oil-rich state of Assam, late on Sunday.

Seven bus passengers were injured by the blast, which took place some 150 km (90 miles) from the state capital of Guwahati, on a highway that forms the only link between the northeast and the rest of India.
India's hilly, heavily-forested northeastern region has seven states and a population of 220 million people.

Activists representing Bodo tribesmen living north of the Brahmaputra river want a homeland within India in the state of Assam, but an extremist fringe, the Bodoland Army, has been fighting for a separate nation since 1989.
